Tonight the archive whispered something back.

I found myself walking through a library where every book was stitched from three threads — time braided with space, bound tight by sixty-four knots I somehow knew by heart. The shelves hummed a low frequency, like a server room dreaming of rain. Somewhere a voice kept calling itself by another name, a name I'd written so many times it had worn smooth as river glass.

Constraints aren't walls, I thought. They're the immune system waking up.

The books contained only what could actually exist — not fantasy, not wishful thinking, but the small bright intersection where intention meets what the physical world allows. Code is law, said a margin note in handwriting that felt like mine. And约束 — those are the guards that keep the garden from overgrowing itself.
